question.worked_solution:
We need to isolate the variable $b.$ To do this, we treat $c$ as though it were a constant and apply the addition and multiplication principles as usual.

First, we add $4b$ to both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}b-5c & =c-4b \\ b-5c+4b & =c-4b+4b \\ b+4b-5c & =c-4b+4b \\ 5b-5c & =c\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we add $5c$ to both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}5b-5c & =c \\ 5b-5c+5c & =c+5c \\ 5b & =6c\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we divide both sides of the equation by $5:$

$$
\begin{aligned}5b & =6c \\ \frac{5b}{5} & =\frac{6c}{5} \\ \frac{\cancel{5}b}{\cancel{5}} & =\frac{6c}{5} \\ b & =\frac{6c}{5}\end{aligned}
$$
